# Tasks Document

Two phases, and the split is not cosmetic: **phase 1 touches no example file and can land whenever it is ready**, while **phase 2 renames files inside two example trees other agents own** and should wait for them. Nothing in phase 2 is a prerequisite for phase 1.

**One thing to know before task 1, because it changes who the work serves.** `ContextOption.unavailable_reason` — added in task 1 — has **two consumers, not one**. This spec needs it for a folder that already holds its registration; `contracts-and-build-hygiene`'s catalog group needs the same field to show ~50 registered placeholder types as visible-but-not-choosable, which is the user's decision on that question. So the field is **the general "offered but not choosable" idiom**, of which the folder case is the first instance, and its comment and its documentation must say so. Written as folder-specific it would have to be widened by the next consumer; written generally it is consumed with no contract change at all.

**Worktree.** `.claude/worktrees/far` — short, because a long worktree name pushes the deepest project paths past `MAX_PATH` and the symptom is `dotnet test` reporting `Zero tests ran` rather than failing the build. Set `MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1` and `DOTNET_CLI_USE_MSBUILD_SERVER=0` before gating, and capture each gate's exit code **into a variable before any pipe** — in a pipeline `$?` is the last command's status, so a crashed or zero-test run reads as green.

**Identity, once, at creation.** `git config --worktree user.name "agent-N-folder-add"` in the worktree the moment you create it. Every command run there inherits it, **merges included** — which is the half `git -c` on `git commit` does not cover, and how a merge came to be authored as another agent today. Read it back with plain `git config user.name` before your first commit in any tree you did not create yourself.

**Specification documents are not worktree work.** This file, its approvals, its snapshots and its implementation logs are written and committed on `develop` in the main checkout with `git -C C:\git\EtAlii.Adp` and an explicit pathspec — the dashboard reads `.spec-workflow/` from there and nowhere else.

**Merging.** Through a **per-agent** scratch worktree, never in place and never a shared name: `git merge` builds its tree from the index, so a foreign staged file blocks it and its failure path dangles other sessions' uncommitted work. Create `.claude/worktrees/mrg<N>`, `merge --no-ff` there, run the four gates on that merged tree, then `git merge --ff-only` from the main checkout. Chain reset, merge, gates and fast-forward in **one** command: develop moves faster than a gate cycle here, and a fast-forward refused an hour later means starting over.

## Phase 1 — the dialog

- [ ] 1. `ContextOption` learns to be offered without being choosable, and to want no name
  - Files: `src/api/context.proto`, `src/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Backend/Context/_Model/ContextOptionNode.cs`, generated code on both sides
  - Add `string name_suppressed_reason = 8` and `string unavailable_reason = 9` to `ContextOption` (fields 1-7 are taken; 8 and 9 are the next free). Mirror both on `ContextOptionNode` at the end of its optional tail.
  - **Each field carries the condition and its explanation in one value.** Non-empty means "this applies", and the string is what the user reads. That is deliberate: it makes it impossible to suppress the name field or grey out an option without saying why, so Requirement 1.3 holds by construction rather than by review.
  - `unavailable_reason` **reuses the name and meaning `ContextAction.unavailable_reason` already carries** (`context.proto:294`, commented there as the disabled item's tooltip) rather than inventing a second idiom for the same thing one message over. Its comment SHALL describe it as the general offered-but-not-choosable idiom and name both consumers, per the note above.
  - `selectable = false` is **not** available for this: it already means "group heading" and overloading it would make a greyed leaf indistinguishable from a category.
  - _Requirements: 1.2, 1.3, 2.1_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: API developer | Task: Add the two per-option fields to ContextOption and mirror them on ContextOptionNode | Restrictions: field numbers 8 and 9; do not touch selectable; no new message and no new RPC; the unavailable_reason comment must describe the general idiom and name both consumers, not the folder case alone; regenerate both sides and keep the four gates green | _Leverage: ContextAction.unavailable_reason at context.proto:294 for the name and meaning | Success: both fields exist on the wire and in the record, the comment scopes the second one generally, and nothing yet sets either. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._

- [ ] 2. One annotation callback replaces the suggestion callback
  - Files: `src/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Backend/Hierarchy/DiagramOptionTree.cs`, `src/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Backend/Context/_Model/ContextOptionAnnotations.cs` (new)
  - Replace `Func<DiagramOrigin, string>? suggest` with `Func<DiagramDefinition, ContextOptionAnnotations>? annotate`, the record carrying `SuggestedValue`, `NameSuppressedReason` and `UnavailableReason`. Taking the **definition** rather than the origin is what lets a caller read `HasFolderSubject` at all.
  - Three per-option values decided in one place instead of three. Groups keep getting nothing, exactly as today.
  - Both existing call sites move: the file-registration branch passes no callback, the folder branch passes one.
  - Tests: a folder-subject definition carries a suppression sentence and no suggestion; a document-subject one carries a suggestion and no suppression; a group carries neither.
  - _Requirements: 1.4, 1.5_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: C# developer | Task: Collapse the option-tree's suggestion callback into one annotation callback taking the DiagramDefinition | Restrictions: groups still receive nothing; no behaviour change for document-subject types, suggestion included; both call sites updated in the same change | _Leverage: DiagramOptionTree.Build's existing per-definition callback and its Suggestion helper | Success: the three per-option values come from one seam, with the three cases tested. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._

- [ ] 3. The provider suppresses the name, and refuses a folder that is already registered
  - Files: `src/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Backend/Hierarchy/AddDiagramContextActionProvider.cs`
  - **Prompt side**: for a folder target, compute the folder's existing folder-subject registration **once**, then annotate — a folder-subject type gets the suppression sentence and no suggestion, and gets an `unavailable_reason` naming the existing file when the folder already holds one. The prompt-level `NameField` stays: file-subject types still need it, and serving both from one dialog is the point.
  - The two sentences are the user-visible half of this spec. Suppression: *"This type registers the folder itself, so the registration is created as `.adp` inside it."* Unavailable: *"This folder is already registered by `structure.adp`"* — naming the file the user can go and look at, bare or legacy-named alike.
  - **Commit side**, inserted into the existing check order rather than rearranging it: after the option resolves, if `definition.HasFolderSubject` then **ignore the submitted name** (log at Warning when non-empty — a stale client should be visible, not silently obeyed), **skip `ValidateName` entirely** (it rejects an empty base name precisely so nothing creates a file called `.adp`, which is the file this path now creates on purpose), re-consult the folder and refuse if it is already registered, and write `DiagramFileName.Extension`.
  - Needs `DiagramFileRouter` as a **required** constructor dependency — the service is registered already, so only the two hand-constructing test files change. Required rather than optional deliberately: an optional router degrades the collision check to "never collides", which is the failure Requirement 2.2 exists to prevent.
  - Tests: the created file is exactly `.adp`; a submitted name is ignored, not honoured; a folder holding a bare `.adp` refuses, and so does one holding a legacy named folder-subject registration; the file-subject path is unchanged, suggestion included.
  - _Requirements: 1.2, 1.3, 1.6, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 5.2_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: C# developer | Task: Annotate the folder prompt and branch the commit for folder-subject types, writing a bare .adp and refusing an already-registered folder | Restrictions: keep the existing check order; ignore rather than refuse a submitted name, and log it at Warning; the router is a required dependency; never overwrite an existing registration | _Leverage: DiagramFileRouter.HasFolderSubjectTypes as the short-circuit before any disk read, and CreateDiagramFileCommand so the new file stays one undo away | Success: the four tests pass and the created file is exactly .adp. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._

- [ ] 4. The dialog shows the sentence where the field was, and greys what cannot be chosen
  - Files: `src/client/src/shell/context/ChoicePromptDialog.tsx`, `src/client/src/shell/context/ChoicePromptDialog.test.tsx`
  - A derived `nameSuppressionFor(options, id)` beside the existing `descriptionFor` and `suggestionFor`. When it returns a sentence, the name row renders **that sentence in the field's place** and submit sends no name — and `canSubmit` must stop requiring a name, or the dialog offers none and then refuses to submit without one.
  - Switching back to a file-subject option restores the field with its `suggestedValue` through the existing `touched` logic — **no round trip, no dialog close** (Requirement 1.5).
  - An option carrying `unavailableReason` renders greyed with its reason and cannot be chosen — including by the double-click-to-submit path, which is easy to miss.
  - Tests: the field is replaced by the sentence and submit carries no name; switching back restores field and suggestion; an unavailable option resists both click and double-click.
  - _Requirements: 1.2, 1.3, 1.5, 2.1_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: React/TypeScript developer | Task: Render the suppression sentence in place of the name field and make an unavailable option unchoosable | Restrictions: no round trip on a selection change; canSubmit must not require a name while the field is suppressed; the double-click submit path must respect unavailability | _Leverage: descriptionFor and suggestionFor as the per-option precedent, and the touched logic that already restores suggestions | Success: three client tests pass and the field never vanishes without a sentence in its place. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._

- [ ] 5. The creation guard, and the read path pinned as tolerant
  - Files: a test beside `AddDiagramContextActionProvider.Tests.cs`, and `EntryDiagramStates.Tests.cs`
  - Assert the Add commit creates exactly `.adp` for a folder-subject type (Requirement 5.2) — the guard against this regressing through the dialog.
  - **Keep** the legacy named shape as coverage of the read path and **add** a bare-`.adp` case beside it. `EntryDiagramStates.Tests.cs:105` reads `DeclaresFolderSubject(registration) => registration == "structure.adp"`, which is a test's stand-in for routing; production routes on the MIME line and the file name never enters the decision. Both shapes must resolve, because **creation is constrained by this spec and reading is not** — a user's existing `infrastructure/structure.adp` keeps opening.
  - _Requirements: 4.1, 4.3, 5.2_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: C# developer | Task: Guard that Add creates a bare .adp, and pin that both the legacy named and the bare registration shapes still resolve | Restrictions: do not tighten the read path; the legacy test case is kept rather than replaced | Success: a regression to a named creation fails the suite, and both read shapes are covered. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._

- [ ] 6. Gate and merge phase 1
  - Four gates, exit codes captured before any pipe, then merge through a per-agent scratch worktree as the preamble describes.
  - **Tell `contracts-and-build-hygiene`'s owner when this lands**, because its catalog group consumes `ContextOption.unavailable_reason` and can start the moment the field exists.
  - _Requirements: 5.3_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Developer | Task: Run the four gates on the merged tree and land phase 1, then notify the second consumer of the new field | Restrictions: judge each gate by an exit code captured before any pipe; read Zero tests ran as a broken build; chain reset, merge, gates and fast-forward in one command | Success: all four gates exit zero on the merged tree and phase 1 is on develop. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._

## Phase 2 — the thirteen renames, after the example trees are free

- [ ] 7. Rename the thirteen named folder-subject registrations
  - Files: seven under `ansible-structure` (six to correct plus `example 1` in both copies), six under `helm-charts` — the exact list is in the requirements' survey
  - `git mv` only: **content byte-identical**, MIME first line and terminator untouched. This is a rename, not a rewrite.
  - **Both copies**, module and showcase. The example-replication guard is gone so they need not move in one commit, but neither copy may be left in the old shape — both are material a reader opens, and a wrong one ships a counter-example.
  - Leave `src/examples/diagrams/ansible-structure/wordpress-nginx/.adp` alone: it is already correct and is the only registration in the tree that was.
  - **Wait for `ansible-refinements` and the helm work.** A rename racing another agent's edits to the same folders is a merge conflict by construction, and waiting costs less than resolving one. Re-measure the survey against the current tip before starting: it was taken at `97f64aee` and confirmed at `e2e854f7`.
  - _Requirements: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 6.1, 6.2_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Developer | Task: Rename the thirteen named folder-subject registrations to a bare .adp in both the module and showcase copies | Restrictions: git mv only, content byte-identical; leave the already-bare one alone; confirm the two example trees are free before starting and re-measure the survey against the current tip | Success: every folder-subject registration in the tree is bare, ExampleRegistrationTests still walks both trees green, and the diagrams still open. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._

- [ ] 8. The shipped-examples guard
  - Files: a test beside `ExampleRegistrationTests`
  - Fail, naming the file, if any folder-subject registration under `src/diagrams/*/examples/` or `src/examples/` carries a name. **Derive folder-subject-ness from the deployed catalog**, never from a hard-coded module list, so a third such module is covered the day it arrives rather than the day someone remembers.
  - _Requirements: 5.1_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: C# developer | Task: Write the guard that fails on a named folder-subject registration in either example tree | Restrictions: derive the folder-subject set from the deployed catalog rather than a module list; the failure message names the offending file and the bare name it should have | _Leverage: ExampleRegistrationTests' existing walk of both trees | Success: reintroducing a named registration fails the suite with its own path in the message. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._

- [ ] 9. Gate and merge phase 2
  - Four gates, then merge as before. Confirm in the running app that a renamed example still opens — routing finds the registration inside the folder either way, and this is the cheap check that says so.
  - _Requirements: 3.4, 5.3_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec folder-add-registration, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Developer | Task: Gate, merge phase 2, and confirm a renamed example still opens in the running app | Restrictions: exit codes captured before any pipe; sign in with the checked-in developer placeholder if the app is needed, and record the check rather than leaving it pending | Success: four gates zero, phase 2 on develop, and one renamed example observed opening. Mark this task in-progress in tasks.md before starting, log the implementation with log-implementation when done, then mark it complete._
